items.title: Choose and document the metadata protection model (decision)
items.context: Decide between Approach A (git add -f + check-ignore guard), B (scaffold/validate the ignore-volatile/track-metadata .gitignore allowlist on init/doctor), C (relocate volatile vs persistent), or a combination. Capture as a decision with >=3 preMortem since this is a critical data-loss path. The chosen model must make the bootstrap git-add behavior and the data-loss protection stance mutually consistent.
items.userSees: A decision record states the chosen protection model and rationale; `lattice story_get` reflects the decision and the PLAN gate passes with >=3 preMortem.

happy.desc: decision_set records chosen=OptAB-combination with rationale making bootstrap git-add and protection stance mutually consistent; story_get reflects it

edge.desc: decision has >=3 preMortem so the high-risk PLAN gate passes (4 recorded)

adversarial.desc: a decision with <3 preMortem or chosen not in options is rejected by decision_set, so the gate cannot be bypassed

items.title: Make worktree bootstrap robust to an ignored story metadata path
items.context: worktree.ts:316 runs `git add .lattice/story/actives/<id>` without -f, which fails with 'paths are ignored' when .lattice is ignored. Implement the chosen model so bootstrap either force-adds with a validated guard or fails with a clear, actionable error/repair instead of an opaque git error.
items.userSees: On a project whose .gitignore would ignore story metadata, worktree bootstrap either succeeds (metadata tracked) or prints a clear remediation message, instead of 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: .lattice'.

happy.desc: On a non-ignoring .gitignore, INIT_CHECK bootstrap force-adds metadata and the scoped commit contains .lattice/story/actives/<id>/index.json (story branch tree non-empty)

edge.desc: On a project whose .gitignore ignores .lattice (broad ignore), bootstrap still succeeds via git add -f (no paths-are-ignored error) AND emits a loud warning pointing at lattice doctor --repair because check-ignore shows the leaf would be cleaned

adversarial.desc: On a project with the negation allowlist (like Orchestrate .gitignore), bootstrap force-add succeeds and the check-ignore guard does NOT warn (leaf re-included, safe) - no false positive

verificationEvidence.note: smoke check: bootstrap non-ignoring .gitignore -> tracked leaf, no warning
smoke check: broad .lattice/ ignore -> dev_start succeeds via git add -f (no paths-are-ignored), leaf tracked, warning present pointing at lattice doctor --repair
smoke check: negation allowlist -> bootstrap succeeds, no false-positive warning (guard probes the leaf not the .lattice prefix)

items.title: Add a doctor check + scaffolding for the track/ignore invariant
items.context: Add a `lattice doctor` check that flags when story metadata is neither tracked nor protected (the data-loss state), and scaffold/repair the correct ignore-volatile/track-metadata allowlist on init or via a repair command, so new projects are safe by default rather than depending on a hand-crafted .gitignore.
items.userSees: `lattice doctor` reports a clear warning (and offers a repair) when story metadata is untracked-and-unignored, instead of the silent data-loss trap; a freshly-initialized project has metadata protected by default.

happy.desc: lattice doctor on a broad-ignore-untracked project prints a clear warning that story metadata is neither git-tracked nor protected, with a repair pointer; --json marks the invariant unsafe

edge.desc: lattice doctor --repair writes the managed ignore-volatile/track-metadata allowlist (idempotent BLOCK markers) so a re-scan reports the invariant safe; second --repair run is a no-op

adversarial.desc: On a safe project (tracked metadata OR negation allowlist like Orchestrate) doctor reports the invariant OK and does NOT false-positive the data-loss warning

verificationEvidence.note: smoke check: doctor on broad-ignore-untracked fixture -> unsafe + remediation text + JSON unsafe flag

items.title: Add regression tests for the data-loss invariant
items.context: Cover: metadata path is tracked (or protected) after bootstrap under both an ignoring and non-ignoring .gitignore; the doctor check detects the unsafe state; bootstrap does not silently leave metadata untracked. Use existing test seams; simulate .gitignore states with fixtures.
items.userSees: `lattice validate` runs the new tests green, proving story metadata cannot end up in the neither-tracked-nor-protected state after bootstrap.

happy.desc: New regression tests run green under lattice validate, covering metadata tracked/protected after bootstrap under both ignoring and non-ignoring .gitignore

edge.desc: A test asserts the doctor predicate flags the broad-ignore-untracked (unsafe) state and clears after repair

adversarial.desc: A test asserts bootstrap does NOT silently leave metadata untracked: force-add path always yields a tracked leaf or a loud warning, never the silent neither-tracked-nor-protected state
